english.title: Perform / agree to perform a function in breach of a Financial Services and Markets Act prohibition order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an individual,

(A)_[performed]_
(B)_[agreed to perform]_

a function in breach of a prohibition order made under section 56(2) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FUNCTION AND NATURE OF THE BREACH..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 56(4) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 56(5) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that In proceedings for an offence under this section it is a defence for the accused to show that he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.
(ii) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the appropriate authority or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
